## Findings

| Protein | Accession | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| **FANCL** (E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase FANCL / FAAP43) | Q9NW38 | 375 aa | **42.904 kDa** |
| **MAS1** (Proto-oncogene Mas) | P04201 | 325 aa | **37.465 kDa** |

**FANCL is heavier** (42.904 vs 37.465 kDa).

### Data anomaly resolved
The UniProt Q9NW38 record contains an internal inconsistency: its header/metadata fields report **281 AA / 32,179 Da**, but the actual stored sequence is **375 aa**. I verified:
- The 375-aa sequence is identical to NCBI RefSeq **NP_060532.2** (FANCL isoform 2) — a real, full-length isoform.
- The 281-aa figure matches a truncated fragment (first 281 residues ≈ 32.15 kDa), not the deposited sequence.
- The UniProt alt-name **"FAAP43"** (Fanconi anemia-associated polypeptide of **43 kDa**) independently confirms the true mass is ~43 kDa, not ~32 kDa.

Had the erroneous 32.18 kDa metadata been used naively, the answer would have flipped to MAS1. The full-length sequence and all independent sources support FANCL as heavier.

<solution>
FANCL (Q9NW38) has a mass of 42.904 kDa, while MAS1 (P04201) has a mass of 37.465 kDa. Therefore FANCL is the heavier protein.
